subject.title: [Bug]: macOS Dashboard window keeps a dead SSH tunnel port after tunnel restart (remote mode)

question: Should the macOS Dashboard recover from a tunnel endpoint change by reinjecting auth and reloading the WebView, or by adding a native-to-web live endpoint update bridge?
rationale: Both approaches fix the stale-port bug, but they trade off implementation size, WebView auth lifecycle risk, and whether a new native bridge becomes a durable product contract.

options.title: Reload on endpoint change
options.body: Subscribe in the Dashboard path, reinject native auth for the new origin, and reload the WebView when the resolved endpoint changes; this is the narrowest repair and easiest to prove.

options.title: Bridge live endpoint updates
options.body: Expose an endpoint-update bridge to the running Control UI so it can reconnect without a full reload, accepting a broader native/web contract.

options.title: Coordinate with tunnel cleanup first
options.body: Wait for the orphaned-tunnel cleanup to reduce port churn, while leaving the open Dashboard window stale-port failure unresolved until the Dashboard behavior is chosen.

recommendation.title: Reload on endpoint change
recommendation.body: Subscribe in the Dashboard path, reinject native auth for the new origin, and reload the WebView when the resolved endpoint changes; this is the narrowest repair and easiest to prove.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the concrete live reproduction and have the strongest current routing signal from merged macOS/dashboard history.
